name: Master of the Ring
epitaph: An open invitational tournament trophy contested across a dozen federations' own talent; Jason Keening won the first edition, Chris Courtade the third, and Victor Frost the seventh.
notes: This collection holds a full broadcast for the tournament's seventh edition and a deciding sixth-edition title match contested on that same broadcast; the first edition's own champion is billed on-air but the tournament that crowned him does not survive here, so no reign is recorded for it.

name: SuperBout
epitaph: An annual grudge-match attraction bout, fought outside the tournament bracket; "Bad Eye" McBaine's seventh-edition win over Eddie Jacobs made him a two-time champion.
notes: Jason Keening is billed on the seventh broadcast as the third SuperBout's own champion, and McBaine as a two-time champion; the second and third editions now survive, contested on the same July 2000 broadcast as the Master of the Ring III tournament final, so three of the seven editions' reigns are recorded.

name: Pentagon Pain
epitaph: A multi-man specialty match run alongside the main tournament; November won its third edition over five other men.
notes: Earlier editions are referenced (this is billed as the third) but do not survive in the held record, so only this reign is recorded.

name: DWF Atlantic Storm Title
epitaph: The DWF's secondary singles title, to be defended on every card under a special stipulation. "Cream of the Crop" Mike Waldrop held it when the federation reopened in August 2001.
